paragraphs: Every day, billions of people wake up hoping for healthier lives, stronger relationships, more meaningful work, more joyful experiences, and a better future for their families.
We believe business can help create that future — not by chasing trends, but by building enduring companies that genuinely improve people's lives.
why_page.belief_intro: Progress should improve the human experience.
beliefs: Technology should make life more human.

philosophy_page.opening: When the history of this century is written...
philosophy_page.q1: Will technology have made us more human?
philosophy_page.answer: Directive 17 exists because we believe the answer should be both.

human_test.intro: Every company begins with one question.

verticals_page.headline: Investing in companies that make people smile, laugh, connect, and live better lives.
intro: Our investment philosophy is simple: We believe making people’s lives better is not only a worthwhile mission, but also an extraordinary investment opportunity.
Below are our nine investment verticals, with examples of the businesses, products, and experiences we intend to invest in and build.

items.name: The Everyday Happiness Economy
bullets: Products and services that create everyday joy.
Businesses that make ordinary moments extraordinary.
Gifting, surprises, and random acts of kindness.
Personal experiences that make people feel special.
Lifestyle brands built around happiness and positivity.
Affordable indulgences and little luxuries.
Subscription businesses delivering recurring happiness.
Innovative products that simplify and improve daily life.

items.name: Human Connection, Belonging & Anti-Loneliness
bullets: Platforms that help people build meaningful friendships.
Experiences that bring strangers together.
Community-building and social engagement businesses.
Corporate employee connection and relocation programs.
Intergenerational friendship and mentorship platforms.
Dating, companionship, and relationship experiences.
Programs combating isolation among seniors, young adults, and families.
Technology that facilitates genuine human interaction rather than replacing it.

items.name: Entertainment, Laughter, Interactive & Immersive Experiences
bullets: Comedy, satire, and humor-driven entertainment.
Live theater, shows, and unique performances.
Interactive and immersive entertainment.
Experiential gaming and audience participation.
Film, television, and original content creation.
Intellectual property development and monetization.
AI-powered entertainment and storytelling.
Family entertainment and attractions.
New technologies that transform audiences into participants.
Entertainment platforms that can scale globally.

items.name: Celebrations & Food
bullets: Businesses that celebrate life’s milestones.
Birthdays, anniversaries, weddings, and unconventional celebrations.
Living celebrations and celebrations of life.
Unique hospitality and dining experiences.
Innovative restaurants, cafés, and food concepts.
Premium food, specialty products, and culinary experiences.
Experiential food retail and e-commerce.
Celebrity chef collaborations and culinary entertainment.
Personalized celebrations and event planning.
Businesses that bring families and friends together around food.

items.name: Sports, Music & Recreation
bullets: Sports leagues, teams, and entertainment properties.
Live music, concerts, and festivals.
Participatory sports and recreational experiences.
New forms of competitive entertainment.
Youth sports and family recreation.
Technology enhancing fan engagement.
Interactive sporting and music experiences.
Outdoor adventures and recreational activities.
Businesses that combine physical activity, community, and fun.

items.name: Technology for the Betterment of Life
bullets: Artificial intelligence that improves human lives.
Technologies that eliminate frustration and complexity.
Personalized AI assistants and concierge platforms.
Preventive health, longevity, and wellness technologies.
Technologies that improve accessibility and independence.
Education and lifelong learning innovations.
Mental wellness and emotional well-being platforms.
Technologies that improve productivity and give people more personal time.
Robotics and automation that enhance quality of life.
Trust, safety, security, and governance technologies that make AI and digital systems more dependable.

items.name: Families, Pets, Babies & The Elderly
bullets: Products and services that strengthen family relationships.
Parenting and early-childhood innovations.
Educational and developmental experiences for children.
Family entertainment and shared activities.
Pet wellness, companionship, and innovative pet services.
Products that improve the lives of older adults.
Aging-in-place and independent living technologies.
Intergenerational experiences and family connections.
Caregiving support and family assistance platforms.
Businesses that improve the quality of life for people and animals at every stage.

items.name: Making the World a Better & Safer Place
bullets: Technologies that protect people and communities.
Public safety and emergency response innovations.
Environmental sustainability and clean living.
Food safety, transparency, and traceability.
Clean water, air quality, and healthier environments.
Technologies that reduce accidents and prevent injuries.
Solutions that improve access to healthcare and education.
Innovations that protect vulnerable populations.
Technologies that strengthen critical infrastructure.
Businesses that solve meaningful societal problems while generating attractive financial returns.

items.name: Crazy Shit (Very Limited)
bullets: Ideas that sound completely insane until they work.
Businesses that create entirely new categories.
Wildly unconventional entertainment concepts.
Products nobody knew they needed.
Technologies that challenge conventional thinking.
Disruptive business models that traditional investors won’t touch.
Experimental ventures with extraordinary upside potential.
Businesses that make people say, “Who the hell thought of that?”
Opportunities where creativity, absurdity, and commercial potential intersect.
Investments that might change the world—or at least make it laugh.
items.note: Investment discipline: This vertical will receive a very limited allocation of capital, with the same rigorous financial and operational underwriting applied to every other investment.

difference.label: The Directive 17 Difference
paragraphs: We are not limited to entertainment, hospitality, technology, sports, or consumer products.
We invest in outcomes that matter to human beings.
We want people to be happier, healthier, safer, more connected, more entertained, and more fulfilled.
difference.questions_intro: Every investment should answer three fundamental questions:
questions: Will this business genuinely make people’s lives better?
Can we build a scalable, financially successful business around that purpose?
Can Directive 17 contribute something meaningful beyond capital?
difference.objective: Our ultimate objective is to generate exceptional financial returns alongside something most investment firms never bother to measure:
closing: And occasionally, we’re going to invest in something so fucking crazy that nobody else would even consider it.
Because sometimes the craziest ideas create the biggest smiles.
